note: HL05 chapter capability ledger. Authored intent, not a derived cache: no validator may rewrite this file. Chapter 1 is deliberately absent — all four of its lessons are still schema v1 with no declared knowledge atoms, so any payoff written for it would be invented rather than derived. That absence is real, measurable debt and must not be papered over with a placeholder.

chapters.title: Give your name
chapters.label: ch:persian-name
chapters.canDo: I can say my name in Persian in one careful sentence, and I can hear the small linking -e that ties the name to its owner.

payoff.summary: One careful sentence with a slot for your own name: esm-e man ... ast, with the spoken ezafe doing the linking.

chapters.title: Ask and Answer Names
chapters.label: ch:fa-ask-and-answer-names
chapters.canDo: I can ask someone's name respectfully with shomâ, answer with my own, and tell them I am pleased to meet them.

payoff.summary: A six-line first meeting: greet, ask the name with respectful shomâ, answer with your own, and acknowledge with khoshvaghtam.

chapters.title: How Are You?
chapters.label: ch:fa-how-are-you
chapters.canDo: I can ask how someone is in careful respectful Persian and answer that I am well, thank you.

payoff.summary: The careful wellbeing exchange in two moves: hâl-e shomâ chetor ast? answered khubam, mamnun.

chapters.title: Take Leave
chapters.label: ch:fa-take-leave
chapters.canDo: I can open a short Persian conversation, check how the other person is, and close it with khodâ hâfez.

payoff.summary: A four-line interaction with a beginning and an end: salâm, the wellbeing check, then khodâ hâfez from both voices.

chapters.title: Name a Verb, Find Its Stem
chapters.label: ch:fa-core-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can name five core Persian verbs in their dictionary form, recognise the -tan/-dan ending that marks any Persian infinitive, and give the present stem that each verb carries beside it.

payoff.summary: The five pairs run back to back from memory — budan, raftan/rav-, âmadan/â-, goftan/gu-, dânestan/dân- — with the infinitive ending named and the stem produced for each.

chapters.title: Four Verbs of the Mind
chapters.label: ch:fa-mind-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can say think, understand, read and write in Persian, give the present stem of each, and tell which of the three ways a Persian verb is built each one uses.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on neveshtan, nevis-, then runs its four verbs back to back — fekr kardan with kon-, fahmidan with fahm-, khândan with khân-, neveshtan with nevis- — and names which is a compound, which hands its stem over free, and which two had to be told. The five pairs from Chapter 6 run after them, so all nine are produced from memory in one sitting.

chapters.title: Taking, Asking, Helping, Loving
chapters.label: ch:fa-doing-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can say take, ask, help and love in Persian, give the present stem where a verb has one, and sort all thirteen verbs I hold into compounds, -idan verbs and inherited verbs.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on dust dâshtan — to have as friend — and its dâr- stem, then runs all thirteen verbs the track has taught: this chapter's four, Chapter 7's four, and Chapter 6's five, each with its stem, sorted into the three shapes a Persian verb can take.
